paragraphs: Ulla, 'who disturbed his mother's ways,' Bava Batra 9a–b, spoke to Rava in R. Elazar's name. Rashi applies this to Rav Sheshet, and mother means nurse. Arukh, R. Tzemaḥ Gaon and Tosafot citing ר״ח [provisionally Rabbenu Ḥananel] apply it to Rav Aḥadvui bar Ammi (see his entry), who caused his mother to uncover her breasts because she had nursed Rav Sheshet. Ran says Rava could not call Rav Sheshet this, since R. Sheshet was far greater. Some read Ila'a; others Ila or Iyula. [Glosses: Ulla. Ḥullin 131b–132a: Rava objected to Ulla, who answered “My teacher, your own argument makes my point” [מטונך, as explained by Rashi]; requires examination, see there; not corrected.]
